text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To achieve our goal of owning the visual presentation of the interface, I propose we prioritize a dark mode design, as it enhances visibility and clarity, especially for users who work in low-light environments. This decision will also contribute to a more enjoyable experience, as it reduces eye strain and creates a sleek, modern aesthetic. By choosing to focus on dark mode, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially increased complexity in our design process, as we'll need to ensure that all elements are legible and visually appealing in a darker color scheme. This added complexity is worth it, as it will ultimately lead to a more engaging and user-friendly interface.

name: Pane
text: I'm not convinced that prioritizing a dark mode design is the best approach, as it may not be suitable for all users, particularly those who work in brightly lit environments or have certain visual impairments. A better alternative might be to offer a customizable theme option, allowing users to choose between light and dark modes, which would provide more flexibility and cater to a broader range of needs. To settle this argument, I'd like to see some user research and feedback on the proposed design, as well as an analysis of the potential impact on our target audience.

name: Facet
text:
Facet: Let’s ship a **single, high-contrast light theme as the default**, with a toggle to switch to a dark theme. This keeps the interface crisp and readable for most users right away—especially in bright offices—while still giving people the choice to reduce eye strain later. The trade-off is that we’re not building a full theme editor upfront, but we can add that later if users ask. The priority is clarity and enjoyment from day one, and a clean light theme delivers that without over-engineering.

name: Pane
text: Pane: While a high-contrast light theme as a default with a dark mode toggle addresses some user needs, it could alienate users who may find high contrast overwhelming or harsh. I suggest we consider a wider range of themes that cater to different lighting conditions and visual preferences right from the start. A/B testing a few options could provide clearer insights into user preferences and settle the debate over which design resonates best.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a **single, adaptable theme system**—defaulting to a balanced, low-contrast light theme with a toggle for dark mode, plus a hidden "customize" option for users who need it.

The result must deliver a clean, readable interface out of the box that respects user choice without overwhelming them. Lumen owns the visual presentation—visibility, liveliness, clarity, and enjoyment—so the theme must feel intentional, not like an afterthought.
